author: Moitra
population: Healthy non-smoking, non-obese (BMI <=30) adult volunteers with normal spirometry; no biomass-fuel or occupational VGDF exposure; n=191 (92 men, 99 women)
statistical_method: Linear regression; all indices ln-transformed except X5 (untransformed); age ln-transformed in some models; GAM used to explore shape, quantile regression with quadratic terms tested but linear models retained
notes: Kolkata cohort measured with Jaeger MasterScreen IOS. Research letter (Int J Tuberc Lung Dis 2020;24(5):536-539); DOI not printed in supplied manuscript PDF, taken from the published citation. Coefficients printed to only 1-3 significant figures; low adjusted R2 (0.01-0.20) and no external validation cohort. Predictions are markedly higher than the European/American equations. Includes Z5 and Fres, which other papers lack. RMSE is on the ln scale for ln-transformed models. Height and weight ranges are not reported. bmi_max=30 is the study exclusion criterion (BMI >30), not an observed maximum; mean BMI 23.5.

author: Oostveen
population: Healthy non-smoking Caucasian adults (88% lifetime non-smokers; ex-smokers <=10 pack-years); n=368 pooled from 5 centres; hospital/university staff and families, plus Busselton Health Study participants in Perth
statistical_method: Multiple linear regression on ln(R), ln(4-X), ln(Fres) and ln(AX); mixed-model ANOVA used to handle centre and frequency effects
device: Multiple: ROS Oscilink (SensorMedics, Bilthoven, Netherlands); i2M (Chess mT, Ghent, Belgium); Jaeger IOS (Jaeger, Wurzburg, Germany); two custom-made setups (Antwerp, Szeged)
notes: Five centres/devices (custom-made, ROS Oscilink, i2M, Jaeger IOS); only the Maastricht centre used IOS (impulse) and the others used pseudorandom-noise forced oscillation, so equations are forced-oscillation rather than IOS-specific; centre dependence found for reactance and for R at 20 and 25 Hz in women. Age range is sex-specific: men 18-84, women 19-81 (age_min/age_max give the overall range). Height ranges: men 1.59-1.97 m, women 1.47-1.88 m; weight ranges: men 54-128 kg, women 43-111 kg. Obesity not an exclusion criterion. Weight (not BMI) used as predictor; BMI-based models did not improve fit. Resistance and reactance in hPa*s/L. Anthropometric ranges are the observed ranges printed with the equations (sex-specific ranges above); BMI range not reported (mean 25.3 women, 26.1 men).

author: Schulz
population: Population-based KORA-F4L and KORA-AGE cohorts; 397 never-smoking lung-healthy adults with normal spirometry from 1990 examined (154 men, 243 women)
statistical_method: Quantile regression (5th, 50th and 95th percentiles) on age, height and weight; linear terms retained over quadratic
notes: Augsburg region, Caucasian; Jaeger MasterScreen IOS. Equations derived from healthy subjects aged 45-89 y but authors recommend applying them only at 45-85 y, 55-100 kg, and heights of 160-190 cm (men) or 145-170 cm (women). Weight enters only the median (50th percentile) models for most indices; 5th and 95th percentile models often omit it. Limits of normal are the 5th/95th percentile equations directly (no RMSE/SD provided). Supplementary Table S1 (additional indices) not included in supplied PDF. Resistance and reactance in kPa*s/L. Height and weight limits are the authors' recommended application limits (not observed minima/maxima); no BMI limits given (5th-95th percentile BMI about 21-35).

author: Berger
population: Healthy asymptomatic lifetime non-smokers living or working in lower Manhattan (World Trade Center Health Registry controls); n=439 (223 men, 216 women); 82.5% (men) and 74.5% (women) white non-Hispanic
statistical_method: Multiple linear regression of ln(IOS parameter) on height and BMI; offsets of +1 (R5-R15, R5-R20) and +4 (X5, X10) added before log transformation
notes: Jaeger IOS. Age was dropped from all equations by the authors (negligible effect), but age ranges are men 21-85 and women 21-76 (age_min/age_max give overall range). Height ranges: men 1.57-2.03 m, women 1.46-1.83 m; BMI range 17-46 kg/m2. Equations may be inaccurate for BMI above about 40 kg/m2 (few subjects, nonlinear obesity effect). No race effect found, so one equation per sex. Weight is needed only to compute BMI. Units are cmH2O*s/L for R and X, and cmH2O/L for AX. Anthropometric ranges are observed ranges across both sexes (men: 1.57-2.03 m, 51.3-170.0 kg, BMI 17.2-44.9; women: 1.46-1.83 m, 43.1-147.4 kg, BMI 16.8-46.6).

author: Gochicoa
population: Healthy non-smokers, mostly Mexican mestizos living in Mexico City; n=830 (54% female) combining three earlier cohorts (children 2.7-15.4 y, children 4.0-12.4 y, adults 20-74 y) and a new cohort aged >14 y; 54.8% were children <=12 y
statistical_method: Multivariate piecewise (segmented) linear regression (R package segmented; breakpoints chosen by BIC) with sex, age, 1/height and 1/BMI; ln model for AX only
device: MS-IOS (Jaeger, CareFusion, San Diego, CA, USA)
notes: Jaeger MS-IOS. Single sex-combined equation set with a sex coefficient (0=female, 1=male); sex, 1/height and 1/BMI coefficients are shared across age segments and only intercept, age coefficient and RMSE differ by segment (two breakpoints for most indices, one for R5-R20). Breakpoint ages differ by parameter. LLN/ULN = predicted -/+ 1.6449*RMSE (AX: applied on the ln scale). Applicability to non-Mexican populations unproven; authors suggest use in other Latin American groups. Includes X15, X20 and (R5-R20)/R5 not in the other papers. Resistance and reactance in kPa*s/L. Anthropometric ranges are overall observed minimum-maximum across all ages (paper Table 1); within any age group the observed range is much narrower (e.g. 86-108 cm at age 2.7-4 y), so extremes are not valid at every age.
